acceptance.sketch: Zoom to three views, run VIEWBACK twice, run VIEWFORWARD once, and assert the display equals the second view while the undo stack length is unchanged.

notes: Added from help page "VIEWFORWARD (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must restore a named saved view into the current viewport, including any background, visual style, live section, UCS or layer state saved with it.

acceptance.sketch: Save a view with a layer state and visual style, change both, run VIEWGO with the view name, and assert view, layer states and visual style are restored.

notes: Added from help page "VIEWGO (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must create projected views from a selected parent model documentation view, inheriting its scale, display settings and alignment, with placement direction choosing the projection type, and must reject out-of-date or unresolved parents.

acceptance.sketch: Select a base view, place a projected view to its right, and assert it has the parent's scale and is aligned horizontally with it; assert an out-of-date parent is refused.

notes: Added from help page "VIEWPROJ (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must let the user set the tessellation count used to display circles, arcs, splines and arced polylines in the current viewport, regenerate the drawing, and store the value in the drawing.

acceptance.sketch: Draw a small circle, set VIEWRES to 5, assert the circle displays as a coarse polygon, then set 20000 and assert it displays smoothly.

notes: Added from help page "VIEWRES (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must open a manager for creating and editing named section view styles that control how section views and section lines look.

acceptance.sketch: Run VIEWSECTIONSTYLE, create a style with a different section line color, apply it to a section view, and assert the section line uses that color.

notes: Added from help page "VIEWSECTIONSTYLE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must let the user choose the active project file that resolves file references for drawings containing views made from Inventor models, taking effect after a restart when such drawings are open.

acceptance.sketch: Run VIEWSETPROJ, pick a project file, and assert the active project path is stored and that unresolved Inventor references resolve through it after restart.

notes: Added from help page "VIEWSETPROJ (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must exit the symbol sketch mode, and when construction geometry was added, prompt the user to save or discard it.

acceptance.sketch: Enter symbol sketch mode, add construction geometry, run VIEWSKETCHCLOSE, and assert a save/discard prompt appears and the choice is applied.

notes: Added from help page "VIEWSKETCHCLOSE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must open a drafting standards dialog that sets default settings used only for newly created base views, leaving existing drawing views untouched.

acceptance.sketch: Change the default projection type in VIEWSTD, create a new base view and assert it uses it, and assert an existing view is unchanged.

notes: Added from help page "VIEWSTD (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must open a sketch environment for a section line or detail boundary where geometric and dimensional constraints and extra construction geometry can be added so the symbol keeps its relation to view geometry on update.

acceptance.sketch: Enter the sketch for a section line, add a coincident constraint to a view edge, update the view after the model changes, and assert the section line stays on that edge.

notes: Added from help page "VIEWSYMBOLSKETCH (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must update selected model documentation views that are out of date relative to their source model, accepting an All entry for every view in the layout and reporting how many were updated.

acceptance.sketch: Make a source model change so a view is out of date, run VIEWUPDATE, select the view, and assert it refreshes and the update count message is shown.

notes: Added from help page "VIEWUPDATE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must restore a maximized layout viewport, returning its center point and magnification to the values before it was maximized.

acceptance.sketch: Maximize a layout viewport with VPMAX, pan and zoom, run VPMIN, and assert the viewport's center and scale equal their pre-maximize values.

notes: Added from help page "VPMIN (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must create multiple viewports from the command line, offering model space or paper space options according to the active space.

acceptance.sketch: Run -VPORTS in model space and assert the model-space prompts appear; run it in a layout and assert the layout viewport prompts appear.

notes: Added from help page "-VPORTS (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Views must support panning and zooming in model space and layouts, with mouse wheel scrolling zooming, wheel dragging panning, and independent current views per model space viewport.

source.ref: About Panning and Zooming in the Current View

acceptance.sketch: In a two-viewport model tab, scroll the wheel over the active viewport and assert only that viewport's view changes.

notes: Added from help page "About Panning and Zooming in the Current View"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Named views capturing magnification, location and orientation must be savable and restorable (VIEW, NEWVIEW) and usable for layout viewports, while ZOOM Previous keeps up to 10 views per viewport for the session only.

acceptance.sketch: Save a named view, pan away, restore the view and assert the view center and scale match; assert ZOOM Previous history is not saved to the file.

notes: Added from help page "About Saving and Restoring Views"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dino 8 must create model documentation base views from 3D models as the first drawing view (set scale, display, orientation, alignment), with projected views inheriting base-view settings by default unless overridden, base views of AutoCAD 3D models including all visible solids and surfaces or selected objects, and Inventor models using chosen view representations.

acceptance.sketch: Create a base view of a 3D solid at 1:2, add a projected view, change the base view scale, and assert the projected view follows; override its scale and assert it no longer follows.

notes: Added from help page "About Base Views"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dino 8 must generate orthogonal and isometric projected drawing views from an up-to-date parent model-documentation view, keeping a parent-child link in which properties default to 'From parent', follow later parent changes until individually overridden, and can be batched with a Defer Updates toggle.

acceptance.sketch: Create a base view, project an orthogonal child, change the base view scale and assert the child's scale follows; override the child's scale and assert further parent changes no longer affect it.

notes: Added from help page "About Projected Views"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dino 8 must mark model-documentation drawing views out of date when the source 3D model changes, update them automatically on drawing open or layout activation when VIEWUPDATEAUTO=1, otherwise flag stale views with markers and a notification for manual update, and allow views that resize to be anchored either at their center or with unchanged geometry fixed in place.

acceptance.sketch: Create a drawing view, edit the source solid, set VIEWUPDATEAUTO=0 and assert the view is flagged stale; run update and assert the flag clears and the view reflects the new geometry, with the Fixed anchor leaving unchanged edges at their prior coordinates.

notes: Added from help page "About Updating Drawing Views"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dino 8 must create model-documentation section views as projected views cut by a section line, with section view styles governing each generated element, inferred constraints (when CONSTRAINTINFER=1) or manual constraints made in a symbol sketch mode that keep the section line positioned relative to view geometry across updates, and per-component participation in the cut.

acceptance.sketch: With CONSTRAINTINFER=1 create a section view through a hole centre, move the hole in the model, update the view, and assert the section line still passes through the hole.

notes: Added from help page "About Section Views"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dino 8 must create model-documentation detail views that show an enlarged portion of a parent drawing view, with detail view styles controlling the boundary and label elements, boundary constraints inferred or manually added in symbol sketch mode so it stays on its features after updates, and behavior that follows parent view rotation.

acceptance.sketch: Create a detail view of a corner at 2:1 scale, update after moving the corner in the model, and assert the detail boundary still encloses the corner and the detail geometry is magnified 2x.

notes: Added from help page "About Detail Views"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dino 8 must support the paper-space plotting workflow: set up a layout's page settings, insert a title block, create viewports on a dedicated layer, set viewport scales, add annotation, and plot at 1:1.

acceptance.sketch: Create a layout with A1 page setup, a title block and a 1:50 viewport, plot it, and assert the output has the specified paper size and a scaled model view.

notes: Added from help page "About Printing From Paper Space"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dino 8 must provide layouts as 2D paper-space sheets, shown as tabs beside Model, containing title blocks, scaled model-space viewports, tables, notes and dimensions, with multiple layouts per drawing.

acceptance.sketch: Add two layout tabs with differently scaled viewports of the same model and assert each displays its own scale and sheet content.

notes: Added from help page "About Layouts"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Dino 8 must split the model-space drawing area into multiple tiled viewports with independent views, and let users store and recall such configurations by name.

acceptance.sketch: Create a four-viewport configuration, save it by name, change to one viewport, restore the name, and assert four viewports return.

notes: Added from help page "About Model Space Viewports"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.
